runs.lastMessage:
Built a basic AI SDK chat app with assistant-ui and localStorage persistence. Here's what you have:

## What's included

**Stack:** Next.js 16, AI SDK v7, `@assistant-ui/react`, `@assistant-ui/ai-sdk`

**Features:**
- Streaming chat via `/api/chat` (OpenAI `gpt-4o-mini` + sample weather tool)
- assistant-ui thread UI with sidebar thread list
- **Multi-thread persistence** in browser `localStorage` (survives reloads)
- Suggested starter prompts

## Key files

| File | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `app/api/chat/route.ts` | AI SDK streaming route |
| `components/chat-provider.tsx` | `useRemoteThreadListRuntime` + `useChatRuntime` |
| `lib/thread-adapter.tsx` | localStorage thread/message adapter |
| `lib/local-storage-db.ts` | Storage helpers |
| `app/page.tsx` | Sidebar + thread layout |

## Run it

1. Add your API key:
```bash
cp .env.local.example .env.local
# Set OPENAI_API_KEY=...
```

2. Dev server is already running at **http://localhost:80** (this environment uses port 80, not 3000).

3. To restart later:
```bash
nohup npm run dev >/tmp/next-dev.log 2>&1 & echo $!
```

## Persistence

Threads and messages are stored under:
- `assistant-ui:threads`
- `assistant-ui:messages:<threadId>`

Create a new thread, send messages, reload the page — your conversations should still be there. For server-side persistence (Postgres, etc.), swap `lib/thread-adapter.tsx` for a database-backed adapter per the [assistant-ui custom persistence docs](https://www.assistant-ui.com/docs/integrations/persistence/custom-adapter).The AI SDK chat app with assistant-ui is built and running.

The dev server is up in the background at **http://localhost:80**. Add your `OPENAI_API_KEY` to `.env.local` (copy from `.env.local.example`) to start chatting. Threads and messages persist in browser localStorage across reloads.

runs.lastMessage:
Good, the dev server is stopped. Everything is set up in `/workspace`.

## Summary

Built a Next.js + assistant-ui chat app with SQLite-backed persistence:

- **Scaffolded** via `assistant-ui@latest create` (default template: OpenAI + AI SDK v7, sidebar thread UI) and added the missing shadcn/assistant-ui components (`thread`, `thread-list`, `threadlist-sidebar`, `breadcrumb`) plus the `lib/utils.ts` `cn()` helper the components needed.
- **Chat backend**: `app/api/chat/route.ts` streams responses via `@ai-sdk/openai` + `streamText`.
- **Persistence** (the part you asked for specifically):
  - `lib/db.ts` — a `better-sqlite3` store (`chat.db`, gitignored) with a `messages` table (`id`, `parent_id`, `format`, `content`).
  - `app/api/history/route.ts` — `GET` lists messages, `POST` appends one.
  - `lib/history-adapter.ts` — a `ThreadHistoryAdapter` using the required `withFormat` pattern so AI SDK `UIMessage`s round-trip through the SQLite rows.
  - Wired into `app/assistant.tsx` via `useChatRuntime({ adapters: { history: historyAdapter } })`.

Verified: `tsc --noEmit` clean, `npm run build` succeeds, dev server serves the page, and `/api/history` round-trips a message through SQLite correctly. I couldn't exercise the actual LLM call since there's no `OPENAI_API_KEY` in this sandbox — you'll need to drop a real key into `.env.local` to test live chat.

**To run it:** add your key to `.env.local` (already copied from `.env.example`) and `npm run dev`. Conversation history now survives page reloads — it's a single persisted thread, not multi-thread cloud sync (the sidebar's "new thread" UI is cosmetic until you add a `RemoteThreadListAdapter`, which is a bigger step up if you want it later).

Built a Next.js chat app in `/workspace` with **assistant-ui** for the UI, the **Vercel AI SDK** calling **Claude Opus 5** (`claude-opus-5`) via `@ai-sdk/anthropic`, and **SQLite** (`better-sqlite3`) for persistence.

**Structure:**
- `app/api/chat/route.ts` — streams responses from Claude
- `lib/db.ts` — SQLite schema (`threads`, `messages`) + helpers
- `app/api/threads/route.ts`, `app/api/history/route.ts` — thread list/create and history load/append
- `lib/history-adapter.ts` — the assistant-ui `ThreadHistoryAdapter` that persists every message to SQLite
- `components/chat.tsx`, `components/sidebar.tsx` — chat pane + thread-switcher sidebar
- `app/thread/[id]/page.tsx`, `app/page.tsx` — per-thread routing, root redirects to the most recent (or a fresh) thread

Multi-thread support is included (sidebar with "New chat" + thread list, each with persisted history that survives reloads) — not just a single persisted conversation.

Verified: `tsc --noEmit` and `npm run build` pass clean; a dev-server smoke test round-tripped a message through SQLite with no errors. One real bug was caught and fixed along the way — the root page was being static-prerendered by Next.js despite depending on live DB state.

**To run it:**
```
cd /workspace
cp .env.local.example .env.local   # add ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-ant-...
npm run dev
```

You'll need a real Anthropic API key in `.env.local` — the app reads `process.env.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` directly, it won't use an `ant`-CLI OAuth profile. Want me to add a `.env.local` for you now if you have a key handy, or wire up something else (e.g. streaming markdown rendering, message editing/branching)?

runs.lastMessage:
Built a basic AI SDK chat app with assistant-ui and SQLite persistence in `/workspace/chat-app`.

## What's included

- **Next.js 16** + **assistant-ui** + **AI SDK v7** streaming chat
- **Multi-thread sidebar** — create, rename, archive, delete conversations
- **SQLite persistence** — threads and messages stored in `data/chat.db`
- **Auto-generated titles** after the first assistant response

## Architecture

| Layer | Implementation |
|-------|----------------|
| UI | assistant-ui `Thread` + `ThreadListSidebar` |
| Runtime | `useRemoteThreadListRuntime` + `useChatRuntime` |
| Persistence | `RemoteThreadListAdapter` + `ThreadHistoryAdapter` with `withFormat` |
| Storage | SQLite via Drizzle ORM + better-sqlite3 |
| AI | `/api/chat` — OpenAI streaming via AI SDK |

## Getting started

```powershell
cd chat-app
cp .env.example .env.local
# Add your OPENAI_API_KEY to .env.local
npm install
npm run dev
```

The dev server is already running at **http://localhost:80** (background via `nohup`).

## Verify persistence

1. Open http://localhost:80
2. Send a message in a new thread
3. Reload the page — the thread list and messages should still be there
4. Check the database: `data/chat.db`

## Key files

- `components/chat-provider.tsx` — wires runtime + persistence
- `lib/thread-adapter.tsx` — client-side persistence adapters
- `app/api/threads/` — thread CRUD + message storage
- `app/api/chat/route.ts` — AI streaming endpoint
- `db/` — SQLite schema and connection

Add your `OPENAI_API_KEY` to `.env.local` before chatting. Without it, the UI and persistence still work, but chat responses will fail.

The signup assistant app is ready at `/workspace/signup-assistant`. The dev server is running at **http://localhost:80**.

## What was built

A split-screen assistant-ui app:

- **Left:** Chat thread where you can ask the assistant to fill or edit form fields
- **Right:** Signup page with **First name** and **Email** inputs

The form is an **app-scoped interactable** (`signupForm`). When it mounts, assistant-ui auto-generates an `update_signupForm` tool the model can call. You can also type directly in the fields — both sides share the same state.

## Try it

1. Add your OpenAI key:
   ```bash
   cp .env.example .env.local
   # Set OPENAI_API_KEY in .env.local
   ```

2. Open http://localhost:80 and try prompts like:
   - "Set my first name to Alex"
   - "Change my email to jane@example.com"
   - "Fill in the signup form with first name Sam and email sam.rivera@example.com"

## Key files

| File | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `app/page.tsx` | Signup form interactable + assistant layout |
| `app/state.ts` | Zod schema for `firstName` and `email` |
| `app/api/chat/route.ts` | AI SDK route with interactable context injection |
| `components/assistant-ui/thread.tsx` | Chat UI built from assistant-ui primitives |

Form state persists across page reloads via `localStorage`.

Built an assistant-ui MCP chat app in `/workspace/mcp-chat-app`. Here's what it includes:

## Features

**MCP server management (add/remove from UI)**
- `McpConfigDialog` in the header — connect presets, add custom servers, disconnect, remove
- OAuth callback at `/mcp/callback`
- Connected tools are exposed to the model as `serverId__toolName` frontend tools

**MCP Apps in chat**
- `McpAppRenderer` renders `ui://` widgets inline in sandboxed iframes
- `McpAppsBrowserHost` routes widget requests through the browser MCP connection (fits user-managed servers)

**Demo MCP server**
- Local server at `http://localhost:8787` with a `show_counter` MCP App (interactive counter widget) plus an `echo` tool

## Project structure

| Path | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `app/providers.tsx` | MCP manager + MCP Apps renderer + chat runtime |
| `app/page.tsx` | Chat thread + MCP servers button |
| `app/api/chat/route.ts` | AI SDK route with `frontendTools()` |
| `lib/mcp-apps-browser-host.ts` | Client-side host for MCP App widgets |
| `server/mcp-server.ts` | Demo MCP server with MCP Apps |

## Run it

```powershell
cd mcp-chat-app
Copy-Item .env.example .env.local
# Set OPENAI_API_KEY in .env.local

npm run dev
```

Or start separately:

```powershell
npm run dev:server   # MCP demo on :8787
npm run dev:web      # Next.js on :3000
```

Dev servers are running at:
- **App:** http://localhost:3000
- **MCP demo:** http://localhost:8787

## Try it

1. Open http://localhost:3000
2. Click **MCP servers** → Connect **Demo MCP Apps**
3. Ask: *"Show me a counter starting at 10 labeled Hello"*
4. The `show_counter` tool should render an interactive MCP App widget in the chat

You can also add any Streamable HTTP MCP server via the **Add server** form (URL + name + auth). Custom servers can be removed; preset connectors can only be disconnected.The MCP chat app is ready in `/workspace/mcp-chat-app`.

It includes:
- **assistant-ui chat** with the thread UI
- **MCP server management** via the **MCP servers** dialog (connect, add custom servers, remove)
- **MCP Apps rendering** inline in chat through `McpAppRenderer`
- A **demo MCP server** on port 8787 with a `show_counter` interactive widget

Dev servers are running:
- App: http://localhost:3000
- MCP demo: http://localhost:8787

To use it, set `OPENAI_API_KEY` in `.env.local`, connect **Demo MCP Apps** from the header, then ask something like: *"Show me a counter starting at 10."*

Your Eve-backed assistant-ui chat app is ready and running.

## What was built

A **Next.js chat app** using:

- **Eve** — durable agent backend in `agent/` (model + system instructions)
- **assistant-ui** — chat UI via `useEveAgentRuntime()` and thread primitives
- **Same-origin setup** — `withEve(withAui(nextConfig))` serves the Eve HTTP channel alongside Next.js

## Key files

| File | Role |
|------|------|
| `agent/agent.ts` | Eve agent config (Claude Sonnet 4.6 via AI Gateway) |
| `agent/instructions.md` | System prompt |
| `app/page.tsx` | Wires `useEveAgentRuntime()` + suggestions |
| `components/assistant-ui/thread.tsx` | Chat UI (messages, composer, suggestions) |
| `components/eve-authorization.tsx` | Connector auth UI for Eve |

## Run it

1. Add your AI Gateway key:

```powershell
Copy-Item .env.local.example .env.local
# Set AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY in .env.local
```

2. The dev server is already running at **http://localhost:80** (logs: `/tmp/next-dev.log`).

3. To restart later:

```powershell
nohup npm run dev >/tmp/next-dev.log 2>&1 & echo $!
```

## Note

The scaffold’s registry thread component was incompatible with the published `@assistant-ui/react` version, so a custom thread was built from assistant-ui primitives instead. It supports markdown, reasoning, tool calls, suggestions, and stop/send controls.Your Eve chat app is built and the dev server is running in the background.

Open **http://localhost:80** to use it. Logs are in `/tmp/next-dev.log`.

To enable real model responses, copy `.env.local.example` to `.env.local` and set `AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY`.

Built a full-stack Mastra + assistant-ui chat app in your workspace.

## What you have

**Frontend (assistant-ui)**
- `app/assistant.tsx` — `useChatRuntime` with `AssistantChatTransport` pointing at `/api/chat`
- `components/assistant-ui/thread.tsx` — chat UI (messages, composer, streaming, copy/regenerate)

**Backend (Mastra)**
- `mastra/agents/chatAgent.ts` — Mastra agent (`openai/gpt-4o-mini`)
- `mastra/index.ts` — Mastra instance registration
- `app/api/chat/route.ts` — streams from `agent.stream()` via `@mastra/ai-sdk` → AI SDK UI message stream

**Config**
- `next.config.ts` — `serverExternalPackages: ["@mastra/*"]` for Mastra on the server
- `.env.example` — template for `OPENAI_API_KEY`
- `README.md` — setup and customization notes

## Run it

1. Add your API key:

```bash
cp .env.example .env.local
# Edit .env.local and set OPENAI_API_KEY
```

2. Start the dev server:

```bash
npm run dev
```

The dev server is already running at **http://localhost:80** (this environment maps Next.js to port 80).

## Architecture

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  UI[assistant-ui Thread] --> Runtime[useChatRuntime]
  Runtime --> API["POST /api/chat"]
  API --> Mastra[Mastra chatAgent]
  Mastra --> Stream[toAISdkStream]
  Stream --> UI
```

The UI uses assistant-ui primitives; Mastra runs in-process in the Next.js API route, following the [full-stack Mastra integration guide](https://www.assistant-ui.com/docs/integrations/frameworks/mastra/full-stack).

To customize the agent, edit `mastra/agents/chatAgent.ts` (instructions, model, tools, memory, etc.). The frontend will pick up changes automatically.The chat app is built and the dev server is running in the background.

Open **http://localhost:80** to use it. Add your `OPENAI_API_KEY` to `.env.local` (see `.env.example`) so the Mastra agent can respond.

Built a LangGraph + assistant-ui stock trading chat app with human-in-the-loop purchase confirmation.

## What's running

| Service | URL |
|---------|-----|
| **Frontend** | http://localhost:80 |
| **LangGraph API** | http://localhost:2024 |

Both servers were started with `nohup` (PIDs in `/tmp/next-dev.log` and `/tmp/langgraph-dev.log`).

## How it works

1. **Chat** — Ask for stock prices or to buy shares (e.g. “Buy 10 shares of TSLA”).
2. **Price snapshots** — `price_snapshot` renders a card with mock quote data.
3. **Purchase approval** — `purchase_stock` shows a confirmation card with **Confirm Purchase** / **Cancel** before the trade executes.
4. **LangGraph interrupt** — The backend pauses at `purchase_approval` until you respond via the tool UI (`addResult({ approve: true/false })`).

## Project layout

```
app/                    # Next.js + API proxy to LangGraph
components/tools/       # Price snapshot & purchase confirmation UIs
backend/src/            # LangGraph stockbroker agent
```

## Before chatting

Add your OpenAI key to `backend/.env`:

```powershell
# backend\.env
OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-your-key-here
```

Then restart the backend:

```powershell
npm run dev:backend
```

## Try it

1. Open http://localhost:80
2. “What's the current price of AAPL?”
3. “Buy 5 shares of TSLA.”
4. Use the confirmation card to approve or cancel the trade

See `README.md` for full setup, architecture notes, and the option to use the hosted demo API instead of the local backend.

Built a React Native weather chat app in `weather-chat-app/` using the official assistant-ui Expo template, with generative UI weather cards.

## What you get

An Expo app (`@assistant-ui/react-native`) that shows weather as **native cards** in the chat thread, not only as text. When you ask “What’s the weather in Tokyo?”, the model calls `get_weather` and the app renders a card with:

- Current temperature and conditions (emoji + label)
- Wind speed
- 5-day forecast row

Weather data comes from [Open-Meteo](https://open-meteo.com/) (no weather API key needed).

## Generative UI pattern

The toolkit in `components/assistant-ui/elements/tools.tsx` uses assistant-ui **Tool UI** (the React Native approach to generative UI):

- `"use generative"` toolkit with a `render` function per tool
- `display: "standalone"` so the weather card sits outside the collapsed tool trace
- `WeatherInstructions` tells the model to use the tool and keep text replies short

## Run it

```bash
cd weather-chat-app
cp .env.example .env
# Add OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-... to .env
npm run start
```

Then press `w` for web, or use a simulator/device.

## Key files

| File | Role |
|------|------|
| `components/assistant-ui/elements/tools.tsx` | `get_weather` tool + `WeatherToolUI` card |
| `components/assistant-ui/weather-instructions.tsx` | System prompt for card-first replies |
| `app/api/chat+api.ts` | AI SDK streaming backend |
| `components/assistant-ui/elements/thread.aui.tsx` | Chat UI + weather suggestion chips |

Try the suggestion chips on the empty screen (“What’s the weather in Tokyo?”) to see the card flow end to end once your OpenAI key is set.

## What you have

A **split-view assistant-ui chat** where the agent renders HTML on a live canvas beside the conversation:

| Left | Right |
|------|-------|
| assistant-ui chat thread | HTML canvas panel (preview + source) |

The agent uses assistant-ui **interactables** — the auto-generated `update_canvas` tool — to set `title` and `html` on the side panel. Visual content stays on the canvas instead of cluttering the chat.

## Try it

1. Add your OpenAI key to `.env.local`:
   ```powershell
   # In html-canvas-chat/.env.local
   OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-...
   ```

2. Open **http://localhost:80**

3. Use the suggestion chips or ask things like:
   - "Draw a bar chart of quarterly revenue"
   - "Build a product card with hover effects"
   - "Show a color palette for a SaaS brand"

## Key files

- `app/page.tsx` — split layout (chat + canvas)
- `app/html-canvas.tsx` — side panel with iframe preview and editable HTML source
- `app/canvas-state.ts` — schema for the canvas interactable
- `app/api/chat/route.ts` — system prompt instructing the agent to use `update_canvas`

## How it works

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  User[You] --> Chat[Chat thread]
  Chat --> API["/api/chat"]
  API --> Model[OpenAI]
  Model --> Tool[update_canvas]
  Tool --> Canvas[HTML canvas panel]
  Canvas --> Preview[Sandboxed iframe]
```

The canvas is editable on your side too — changes sync back to the model on your next message.

Built a Claude-like chat app in `/workspace/claude-chat` using assistant-ui. Here's what you get:

## Layout

```
┌─────────────────┬──────────────────────┬─────────────────────┐
│  Conversations  │       Chat           │    Artifacts        │
│  (thread list)  │   (messages + input) │  (preview + code)   │
└─────────────────┴──────────────────────┴─────────────────────┘
```

## Features

- **Conversation sidebar** — new thread, search, rename, archive, delete (via `ThreadList`)
- **Chat thread** — streaming messages with follow-up suggestions
- **Artifacts panel** — HTML artifacts with live preview, source editing, and version history (Claude Artifacts-style)

## Getting started

1. Add your OpenAI API key:

```bash
cd claude-chat
cp .env.example .env
# Set OPENAI_API_KEY in .env
```

2. The dev server is already running at **http://localhost:80** (this environment uses port 80 instead of 3000).

3. Try prompts like:
   - *"Create a calculator app with HTML and JavaScript"*
   - *"Build a beautiful landing page for a coffee shop"*

When an artifact is generated, click **Open workbench** to preview and edit it in the side panel.

## Project structure

| File | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `app/page.tsx` | Three-column layout: sidebar + chat + artifacts |
| `app/artifact-surface.tsx` | Artifacts workbench and inline trigger cards |
| `app/toolkit.tsx` | Interactable artifact tool for the AI |
| `app/api/chat/route.ts` | Streaming chat API (OpenAI via AI SDK) |
| `components/assistant-ui/elements/` | Thread and thread-list UI components |

See `README.md` for full setup and usage details.

Built a **LangGraph + assistant-ui stock trading chat app** with human-in-the-loop trade confirmation. It’s based on the [assistant-ui stockbroker example](https://github.com/assistant-ui/assistant-ui-stockbroker), simplified to use mock market data so you only need an OpenAI key.

## What you get

- **Chat UI** — assistant-ui thread with suggested prompts
- **Stock tools** — price lookup, company info, and buy orders
- **Trade confirmation** — purchases pause at an approval card; nothing executes until you click Confirm or Reject

## Project structure

```
/workspace/
├── backend/          # LangGraph agent (port 2024)
│   └── src/
│       ├── index.ts  # Graph with purchase_approval interrupt
│       └── tools.ts  # Mock stock data + purchase_stock tool
└── frontend/         # Next.js + assistant-ui (port 3000)
    └── components/tools/purchase-stock/  # Approval UI
```

## How confirmation works

1. User asks to buy stock → agent calls `purchase_stock`
2. Graph routes to `prepare_purchase_details` → `purchase_approval`
3. `purchase_approval` throws `NodeInterrupt` until you respond
4. assistant-ui shows a **Confirm Transaction** card
5. **Confirm** → trade executes; **Reject** → agent acknowledges cancellation

## Running it

Both servers are already running:
- **Frontend**: http://localhost:3000
- **LangGraph API**: http://localhost:2024

Set your OpenAI key in `backend/.env`:

```bash
OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-your-key-here
```

Then restart the backend:

```powershell
cd backend; pnpm dev
```

## Try it

1. “What’s the price of Apple stock?”
2. “Buy 2 shares of Tesla”
3. Review the confirmation card and click **Confirm** or **Reject**

Mock tickers: **AAPL, TSLA, MSFT, GOOGL, AMZN, NVDA, META, MCD**

See `README.md` for full setup details.

Built a React Native weather chat app in `weather-chat-app/` using assistant-ui and generative UI.

## What you get

An Expo app where asking *"What's the weather in Tokyo?"* triggers:

1. **`get_weather`** — fetches live data from Open-Meteo (no weather API key)
2. **`present`** — composes a native **WeatherCard** via generative UI (not just text)

The card shows current temperature, conditions, wind, and a 5-day forecast with emoji icons.

## Architecture

| Layer | Role |
|---|---|
| `components/assistant-ui/elements/tools.tsx` | `"use generative"` toolkit: `get_weather` + `present` |
| `components/generative-ui/` | RN components the model can compose (`WeatherCard`, `Card`, `Row`, `Fact`, `Text`) |
| `lib/weather.ts` | Open-Meteo geocoding + forecast |
| `app/api/chat+api.ts` | Streaming chat API with a system prompt that steers weather → card |

## Run it

```powershell
cd weather-chat-app
npm install
Copy-Item .env.example .env
# Add your OPENAI_API_KEY to .env
npm run start
```

Then open iOS, Android, or web and try the weather suggestions.

## Example flow

```
User: "What's the weather in Tokyo?"
  → get_weather({ location: "Tokyo" })
  → present({ $type: "WeatherCard", location: "Tokyo", temperature: 72, ... })
  → Native WeatherCard renders in the thread
```

The app is in `/workspace/weather-chat-app`. See `README.md` for full setup and project structure.

Built a **Canvas Chat** app in `/workspace/canvas-chat` using assistant-ui. Here's what you get:

## Layout

- **Left (60%)** — chat thread with streaming responses
- **Right (40%)** — HTML canvas the agent controls

## How the canvas works

The side panel is an **app-scoped interactable** (`canvas`). When it mounts, assistant-ui auto-registers an `update_canvas` tool so the model can set `title` and `html`. The API route injects the current canvas state into each message via `unstable_injectInteractableContext`, so the agent always knows what's on screen.

HTML renders in a **sandboxed iframe** (`allow-scripts` only).

## Get started

```bash
cd canvas-chat
cp .env.example .env.local
# Add OPENAI_API_KEY to .env.local
npm run dev
```

Open [http://localhost:3000](http://localhost:3000) (in this environment the dev server bound to port 80).

## Try it

- "Draw a bar chart comparing Q1–Q4 revenue"
- "Show a system architecture diagram for a Next.js app"
- "Create a landing page mockup for a coffee shop"

The agent should update the canvas while keeping chat replies short.

## Key files

| File | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `app/assistant.tsx` | Split layout + interactables config |
| `components/canvas/html-canvas-panel.tsx` | Side canvas panel |
| `lib/canvas-schema.ts` | Zod schema for canvas state |
| `app/api/chat/route.ts` | AI route with canvas system prompt |

The dev server is already running in the background. If you want changes — different styling, a literal `<canvas>` element for drawing, or persistence across reloads — say what you'd like next.The **Canvas Chat** app is ready in `/workspace/canvas-chat`.

The dev server is running in the background and responding with HTTP 200. In this environment it’s on **http://localhost:80** (not 3000).

To use it locally:
1. `cd canvas-chat`
2. Copy `.env.example` to `.env.local` and set `OPENAI_API_KEY`
3. Open the app and ask for a chart, diagram, or layout — the agent should render it on the side canvas via `update_canvas`

- **Next.js + Eve plugin** via `withEve(withAui(...))` in `next.config.ts`
- **Chat UI** in `app/page.tsx` using `useEveAgentRuntime()` and the prebuilt `Thread` component
- **Tool/reasoning/attachment UI** under `components/assistant-ui/`

## Before you chat

Add your Vercel AI Gateway key to `.env.local`:

```powershell
# In eve-chat/.env.local
AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY=your-api-key
```

Get a key at [vercel.com/ai-gateway](https://vercel.com/ai-gateway).

## Run it

```powershell
cd eve-chat
npm run dev
```

The dev server is already running in this environment at **http://localhost:80** (because `PORT=80` is set here). Logs: `/tmp/next-dev.log`.

## Architecture

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  Browser["Browser (Thread UI)"] --> Runtime["useEveAgentRuntime()"]
  Runtime --> Eve["Eve HTTP channel (same origin)"]
  Eve --> Agent["agent/agent.ts"]
  Agent --> Gateway["Vercel AI Gateway"]
```

- `useEveAgentRuntime()` bridges Eve sessions into assistant-ui’s runtime
- Eve handles durable sessions, streaming, and tool execution
- The `Thread` component renders messages, reasoning blocks, tool calls, and follow-up suggestions

See [`README.md`](/workspace/eve-chat/README.md) for project layout and scripts. To customize the agent, edit `agent/instructions.md` or extend `agent/agent.ts`.

Your **LangGraph + assistant-ui stockbroker app** is in `/workspace/stockbroker`. Both servers are running.

## What was built

A stock trading chat assistant where:

1. The **LangGraph agent** researches stocks (prices, financials) via tools
2. When you ask to buy shares, it routes to a **`purchase_approval` node** that throws a `NodeInterrupt`
3. A **confirmation card** appears in the chat — the trade only runs after you click **Confirm Purchase**

## Project structure

| Component | Location |
|-----------|----------|
| LangGraph workflow with HITL interrupt | `backend/agent.ts` |
| Stock tools (mock data by default) | `backend/tools.ts` |
| LangGraph runtime wiring | `app/MyRuntimeProvider.tsx` |
| Purchase confirmation UI | `components/tools/purchase-stock/` |
| API proxy to LangGraph dev server | `app/api/[..._path]/route.ts` |

## Running locally

Servers are already up:

- **Frontend:** http://localhost:80
- **LangGraph API:** http://localhost:2024

Add your OpenAI key to `.env.local`:

```powershell
cd stockbroker
# Edit .env.local and set OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-...
```

Then try: **"Buy 5 shares of Tesla stock at the current price."** — you should see the confirmation card before anything executes.

Restart dev servers:

```powershell
cd stockbroker
nohup npm run dev >/tmp/stockbroker-dev.log 2>&1 & echo $!
```

## How confirmation works

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A[User asks to buy] --> B[Agent calls purchase_stock]
  B --> C[prepare_purchase_details]
  C --> D[purchase_approval - NodeInterrupt]
  D --> E[Confirmation UI in chat]
  E -->|Confirm| F[execute_purchase]
  E -->|Cancel| G[Back to agent]
```

The UI uses `makeAssistantToolUI` with `addResult(JSON.stringify({ approve: true/false }))` to resume the interrupted graph — the same pattern as the [official stockbroker tutorial](https://www.assistant-ui.com/docs/runtimes/langgraph/tutorial/part-3).

See `README.md` in the project for full setup details, including optional real market data via `FINANCIAL_DATASETS_API_KEY`.The stockbroker app is ready in `/workspace/stockbroker` and both servers are running:

- **Chat UI:** http://localhost:80  
- **LangGraph API:** http://localhost:2024  

To use it, add your `OPENAI_API_KEY` to `stockbroker/.env.local`, then try something like: *"Buy 5 shares of Tesla at the current price."* You should get a confirmation card before any trade runs.

## What you get

An **Expo** app (`@assistant-ui/react-native`) with:

- Chat UI — drawer thread list, composer, streaming messages

## Weather generative UI

The toolkit co-locates schema, execute, and render in one file:

```304:334:/workspace/weather-chat/components/assistant-ui/tools.tsx
export default defineToolkit({
  get_weather: {
    description:
      "Look up current weather and a 5-day forecast for a city or location. Always use this tool when the user asks about weather.",
    parameters: z.object({
      location: z
        .string()
        .describe("City or place name, e.g. San Francisco or Tokyo"),
    }),
    execute: async (args: { location: string }) => {
      "use client";
      return lookupWeather(args.location);
    },
    render: WeatherToolUI,
  },
});
```

`WeatherToolUI` renders a card with current conditions and a forecast row. The server streams tool calls; the client runs the tool and paints the card inline in the thread.

runs.lastMessage:
Built a polished Northstar trading copilot with:

- assistant-ui chat runtime and custom trading workspace
- LangGraph state graph with an actual confirmation interrupt
- Buy order parsing for supported demo symbols
- Review card with quantity, price, total, and market order type
- Confirm/cancel actions before execution
- Portfolio, holdings, watchlist, and brokerage status panels
- Responsive mobile navigation

Key files:

- [Trading UI]( /workspace/app/trading-assistant.tsx )
- [LangGraph workflow]( /workspace/lib/trading-graph.ts )
- [Chat API route]( /workspace/app/api/chat/route.ts )
- [README]( /workspace/README.md )

Verified with `npx tsc --noEmit`, `npm run build`, and manual proposal → approval API tests. The dev server is not left running.

runs.lastMessage:
Built a polished Vite + React assistant-ui chat app from scratch.

Highlights:
- Uses `@assistant-ui/react` primitives and `useLocalRuntime` per the current assistant-ui setup. [assistant-ui docs](https://www.assistant-ui.com/docs/runtimes/custom/local-runtime)
- Dark sidebar with conversations, recent chats, projects, saved items, and workspace profile.
- Responsive conversation canvas with assistant/user messages, feedback actions, status indicator, suggestions, and composer.
- Local demo adapter works without API keys and is easy to replace with a real backend.
- No Next.js involved.

Key files:

- [src/App.tsx](/workspace/src/App.tsx)
- [src/main.tsx](/workspace/src/main.tsx)
- [src/styles.css](/workspace/src/styles.css)
- [package.json](/workspace/package.json)

Verified with:

```bash
npm run build
```

Build succeeds. Start it with:

```bash
npm run dev
```

Built a polished responsive weather chat app in `/workspace`.

Key features:

- assistant-ui `ThreadPrimitive` and `ComposerPrimitive`
- Generative weather card with current conditions, wind, rain, UV, and 5-day forecast
- Live Open-Meteo weather lookup with graceful fallback data
- Responsive sidebar, recent chats, suggestions, mobile menu, composer controls
- Custom Skyline visual styling

- [app/chat-shell.tsx](/workspace/app/chat-shell.tsx)
- [app/runtime-provider.tsx](/workspace/app/runtime-provider.tsx)
- [app/api/weather/route.ts](/workspace/app/api/weather/route.ts)
- [app/globals.css](/workspace/app/globals.css)

runs.lastMessage:
Built an Eve-backed assistant-ui chat app from scratch.

Highlights:
- Polished responsive dark UI with sidebar, recent conversations, onboarding state, suggestions, and composer.
- Real Eve runtime via `useEveAgentRuntime()`.
- Eve/Next integration configured with `withEve(withAui(...))`.
- Markdown assistant responses via `@assistant-ui/react-markdown`.
- New conversation reset and attachment support.
- Added `remark-gfm`.

Key files:
- [app/page.tsx](/workspace/app/page.tsx)
- [components/assistant-ui/thread.tsx](/workspace/components/assistant-ui/thread.tsx)
- [app/globals.css](/workspace/app/globals.css)
- [agent/agent.ts](/workspace/agent/agent.ts)

Validation passed:

```bash
npm run lint
npm run build
```

Add `AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY` to `.env.local` before running. The dev server could not stay up in this container because Eve requires Node 24+, while the environment has Node 22. The Eve wiring follows the [official assistant-ui Eve quickstart](https://www.assistant-ui.com/docs/runtimes/eve/quickstart).

runs.lastMessage:
Built the chat app in `/workspace`.

Key pieces:

- Responsive Relay chat UI with assistant-ui primitives
- Mastra `relayAgent` backend
- Streaming `/api/chat` route via AI SDK
- Suggestion cards, thread sidebar, composer, share toast, responsive mobile layout
- `.env.example` with `OPENAI_API_KEY`

Files:

- [components/chat-workspace.tsx](/workspace/components/chat-workspace.tsx)
- [app/api/chat/route.ts](/workspace/app/api/chat/route.ts)
- [mastra/agents/relay-agent.ts](/workspace/mastra/agents/relay-agent.ts)
- [mastra/index.ts](/workspace/mastra/index.ts)

The implementation follows assistant-ui’s documented Mastra full-stack streaming pattern. [Docs](https://www.assistant-ui.com/docs/integrations/frameworks/mastra/full-stack)

Verified:

- `npm run typecheck`
- `npm run build`
- `/` returns 200
- `/api/chat` returns streaming responses

No dev server was left running.
